## Why this document exists

`aeolus` aims to be a Python-native replacement for core openair workflows.
For users to trust that, "works like openair" can't just be a design claim —
it has to be measurable. This page shows the evidence.

Every metric on this page is computed two ways on the same input data:

1. **R openair** computed the reference values on the pinned version shown
   in _Provenance_ below. Outputs are checked into the aeolus repo at
   `tests/fixtures/openair/`.
2. **aeolus** computes the same metrics from the same raw data.

The two are then compared value-by-value. A failing comparison fails CI,
and this document will not render until parity is restored.

::: {.callout-note}
The R code on this page is shown for documentation — it isn't executed
when the page renders, so you don't need R or openair installed to read
this. See `scripts/validation/generate_openair_fixtures.R` for the exact
commands that produced the reference fixtures.
:::

## Provenance

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: provenance
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

FIXTURES = Path("../../tests/fixtures/openair")
prov = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "provenance.csv")
prov.T.rename(columns={0: "value"}).style.set_caption("Fixture provenance")
```

## Dataset

**Site**: London Marylebone Road (MY1), AURN.

**Period**: calendar year 2023 (8,760 hourly observations).

**Pollutants**: NO₂, PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃.

MY1 is a well-known kerbside site with dense coverage of all regulatory
pollutants, chosen as a canonical comparison dataset because it exercises
every metric on realistic roadside concentrations.

## Loading the same raw input in both environments

The R reference — not executed here, shown for documentation:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(openair)
raw <- importAURN(site = "my1", year = 2023)
```

The Python side reads the same raw data produced by `importAURN`, via
the CSV fixture:

```{python}
#| label: load-raw
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

FIXTURES = Path("../../tests/fixtures/openair")
raw = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_raw.csv")
raw["date"] = pd.to_datetime(raw["date"], utc=True)
raw.head()
```

## Metric 1 — daily mean with 75% data-capture threshold

The standard LAQM annual-report metric: the mean of hourly values within
each calendar day, with the day dropped (NaN) if fewer than 75% of hours
are valid.

### Idiomatic usage

Each tool consumes data in its native shape and produces a daily summary
with one function call:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
**R openair**

```r
daily <- timeAverage(
  aurn,
  avg.time = "day",
  data.thresh = 75
)
```

openair expects wide-format input
(one column per pollutant).
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**aeolus**

```python
daily = time_average(
    aurn,
    freq="D",
    data_thresh=0.75,
)
```

aeolus expects long-format input
(one row per measurement).
:::

::::

The only difference in practice is input shape — both calls take the
same parameters and produce an equivalent daily summary. aeolus uses
long format by design (we think it scales better to multi-source,
multi-pollutant workflows), not because we're translating openair.

### Comparison scaffolding

For the strict numerical parity check, we need to run the _same bytes_
through both tools and align outputs. The code below reshapes openair's
wide-format raw data into aeolus's long-format schema, calls
`time_average`, then pivots the result back to wide so we can diff it
against the openair reference cell-by-cell. This is test plumbing, not
idiomatic aeolus code.

```{python}
#| label: aeolus-daily
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the reshape + pivot plumbing"
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from aeolus.metrics import time_average

# Reshape openair's wide-format raw data into aeolus's long-format schema
pollutants = ["no2", "pm2.5", "pm10", "o3"]
long = raw.melt(
    id_vars=["date", "site", "code"],
    value_vars=pollutants,
    var_name="measurand",
    value_name="value",
)
long["measurand"] = long["measurand"].map(
    {"no2": "NO2", "pm2.5": "PM2.5", "pm10": "PM10", "o3": "O3"}
)
aeolus_input = pd.DataFrame({
    "site_code": long["code"],
    "date_time": long["date"],
    "measurand": long["measurand"],
    "value": pd.to_numeric(long["value"], errors="coerce"),
    "units": "ug/m3",
    "source_network": "AURN",
    "ratification": "None",
    "created_at": datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
})

# The actual aeolus call — everything above is format-alignment plumbing
aeolus_daily_long = time_average(aeolus_input, freq="D", data_thresh=0.75)

# Pivot aeolus's long output back to wide to match openair's shape
aeolus_daily = aeolus_daily_long.pivot_table(
    index="date_time", columns="measurand", values="value", aggfunc="first"
).reset_index().rename(columns={"date_time": "date"})
aeolus_daily = aeolus_daily.rename(
    columns={"NO2": "no2", "PM2.5": "pm2.5", "PM10": "pm10", "O3": "o3"}
)
```

### Numerical comparison

```{python}
#| label: compare-daily
import numpy as np

openair_daily = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_daily_mean_thresh75.csv")
openair_daily["date"] = pd.to_datetime(openair_daily["date"], utc=True)

merged = aeolus_daily.merge(
    openair_daily, on="date", suffixes=("_aeolus", "_openair")
)

rows = []
for p in pollutants:
    a = merged[f"{p}_aeolus"].to_numpy()
    o = merged[f"{p}_openair"].to_numpy()
    both = ~np.isnan(a) & ~np.isnan(o)
    diffs = np.abs(a[both] - o[both])
    rows.append({
        "pollutant": p.upper(),
        "n_days_compared": int(both.sum()),
        "n_days_nan_both": int((np.isnan(a) & np.isnan(o)).sum()),
        "max_abs_diff": f"{diffs.max():.2e}" if len(diffs) else "—",
        "mean_abs_diff": f"{diffs.mean():.2e}" if len(diffs) else "—",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

All four pollutants match to ~10⁻¹⁴ µg/m³ — floating-point noise level,
indicating bit-identical algorithms modulo the order of summation.

### Time-series overlay

```{python}
#| label: plot-overlay
#| fig-cap: "aeolus vs openair daily NO₂ — red dots visible only where values disagree."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
ax.plot(merged["date"], merged["no2_openair"], label="openair", lw=1.2)
ax.plot(merged["date"], merged["no2_aeolus"], label="aeolus", lw=1.2, linestyle="--")

disagreements = np.abs(merged["no2_aeolus"] - merged["no2_openair"]) > 1e-6
if disagreements.any():
    ax.scatter(
        merged.loc[disagreements, "date"],
        merged.loc[disagreements, "no2_aeolus"],
        color="red", s=30, zorder=5, label="disagreement (>1e-6)",
    )

ax.set_ylabel("NO₂ (µg/m³)")
ax.set_xlabel("Date")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Metric 2 — monthly mean

Same pipeline as daily, different frequency. `aeolus.time_average(freq="MS")`
vs `openair::timeAverage(avg.time="month")`.

```{python}
#| label: compare-monthly
import numpy as np

openair_monthly = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_monthly_mean_thresh75.csv")
openair_monthly["date"] = pd.to_datetime(openair_monthly["date"], utc=True)

aeolus_monthly_long = time_average(aeolus_input, freq="MS", data_thresh=0.75)
aeolus_monthly = aeolus_monthly_long.pivot_table(
    index="date_time", columns="measurand", values="value", aggfunc="first"
).reset_index().rename(columns={"date_time": "date"}).rename(
    columns={"NO2": "no2", "PM2.5": "pm2.5", "PM10": "pm10", "O3": "o3"}
)

merged_m = aeolus_monthly.merge(openair_monthly, on="date", suffixes=("_aeolus", "_openair"))

rows = []
for p in pollutants:
    a = merged_m[f"{p}_aeolus"].to_numpy()
    o = merged_m[f"{p}_openair"].to_numpy()
    both = ~np.isnan(a) & ~np.isnan(o)
    diffs = np.abs(a[both] - o[both])
    rows.append({
        "pollutant": p.upper(),
        "n_months_compared": int(both.sum()),
        "max_abs_diff": f"{diffs.max():.2e}" if len(diffs) else "—",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

## Metric 3 — Theil-Sen trend

`aeolus.trend()` computes a non-parametric trend using the Theil-Sen
estimator (median of pairwise slopes) with a Mann-Kendall significance
test. openair's `TheilSen()` does the same, with one important
implementation difference:

- **openair** bootstraps confidence intervals (1000 samples by default)
- **aeolus** uses `scipy.stats.theilslopes`, which returns analytical CIs

So we expect close agreement on the slope (a deterministic median) and
the significance conclusion at α=0.05, but CI bounds will differ by
method. This is documented divergence, not a bug.

Trend analysis needs several years of data to be meaningful, so this
section uses a wider time window: Marylebone Road, 2020-2023.

```{python}
#| label: load-trend-data
trend_raw = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2020_2023_raw.csv")
trend_raw["date"] = pd.to_datetime(trend_raw["date"], utc=True)
trend_long = trend_raw.melt(
    id_vars=["date", "site", "code"],
    value_vars=["no2", "pm2.5", "pm10", "o3"],
    var_name="measurand", value_name="value",
)
trend_long["measurand"] = trend_long["measurand"].map(
    {"no2": "NO2", "pm2.5": "PM2.5", "pm10": "PM10", "o3": "O3"}
)
trend_input = pd.DataFrame({
    "site_code": trend_long["code"],
    "date_time": trend_long["date"],
    "measurand": trend_long["measurand"],
    "value": pd.to_numeric(trend_long["value"], errors="coerce"),
    "units": "ug/m3",
    "source_network": "AURN",
    "ratification": "None",
    "created_at": datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
})
```

```{python}
#| label: compare-trend
from aeolus.metrics import trend

openair_trend = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2020_2023_trend_theilsen.csv")

rows = []
for p in ["NO2", "PM2.5", "PM10", "O3"]:
    aeolus_tr = trend(trend_input, pollutant=p, avg_time="month", deseason=False)
    ref = openair_trend[openair_trend["pollutant"] == p].iloc[0]
    rows.append({
        "pollutant": p,
        "aeolus slope": f"{aeolus_tr.slope:+.4f}",
        "openair slope": f"{ref['slope']:+.4f}",
        "slope diff": f"{abs(aeolus_tr.slope - ref['slope']):.2e}",
        "aeolus p": f"{aeolus_tr.p_value:.3f}",
        "openair p": f"{ref['p_value']:.3f}",
        "significant @0.05": (
            "yes" if (aeolus_tr.p_value < 0.05) == (ref["p_value"] < 0.05)
            else "DISAGREE"
        ),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

All four pollutants agree on slope to ~10⁻³ µg/m³/year — within the noise
expected from how each tool represents time as a fractional-year
coordinate (aeolus: `year + dayofyear/365.25`; openair: `days-since-epoch /
365.25`). Both tools reach the same significance conclusion in every case.

::: {.callout-note}
### Bug found via this validation

The first run of this comparison surfaced a subtle bug in
`aeolus.time_average`: the data-capture threshold denominator used a
fixed 30-day approximation for monthly aggregation, so 31-day months
got an inflated capture score (~3% higher than reality). In practice,
this caused one July 2021 O3 month with 73.9% capture to be incorrectly
included (it should have been dropped at the LAQM 75% threshold). The
fix switches to per-bin calendar-aware expected counts — now aeolus
correctly matches openair on which months cross the threshold. Fixed
in the same PR as this validation.
:::

## Metric 4 — timeVariation decomposition

`openair::timeVariation()` decomposes a time series into diurnal (hour of
day), day-of-week, and monthly components with confidence bands. aeolus
computes the same underlying aggregates inside `plot_diurnal`,
`plot_weekly`, and `plot_monthly`. We validate the numerical means — CI
bounds differ by estimation method (openair bootstraps, aeolus uses a
t-distribution approximation), but the means are unambiguous arithmetic
groupbys and should match exactly.

```{python}
#| label: compare-timevariation
no2 = aeolus_input[aeolus_input["measurand"] == "NO2"].copy()
no2["date_time"] = pd.to_datetime(no2["date_time"], utc=True)

# Aeolus-convention aggregations (matching internal groupby in viz/plots.py)
hour_mean = no2.groupby(no2["date_time"].dt.hour)["value"].mean()
# openair wkday: Mon=1..Sun=7; pandas dayofweek: Mon=0..Sun=6
day_mean = no2.groupby(no2["date_time"].dt.dayofweek + 1)["value"].mean()
month_mean = no2.groupby(no2["date_time"].dt.month)["value"].mean()

openair_hour = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_timevariation_hour.csv")
openair_day = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_timevariation_day.csv")
openair_month = pd.read_csv(FIXTURES / "aurn_my1_2023_timevariation_month.csv")

def _max_diff(aeolus_series: pd.Series, openair_df: pd.DataFrame, key: str) -> float:
    merged = aeolus_series.reset_index().merge(
        openair_df[[key, "Mean"]], left_on=aeolus_series.index.name, right_on=key
    )
    return float((merged["value"] - merged["Mean"]).abs().max())

pd.DataFrame([
    {"panel": "hour-of-day (0-23)",     "n_bins": 24, "max_abs_diff": f"{_max_diff(hour_mean, openair_hour, 'hour'):.2e}"},
    {"panel": "day-of-week (Mon=1..Sun=7)", "n_bins": 7,  "max_abs_diff": f"{_max_diff(day_mean, openair_day, 'wkday'):.2e}"},
    {"panel": "month (1-12)",           "n_bins": 12, "max_abs_diff": f"{_max_diff(month_mean, openair_month, 'mnth'):.2e}"},
])
```

All three decompositions agree to floating-point noise — the underlying
arithmetic mean groupby is the same convention in both tools.

## Status

| Metric | Tolerance | Status |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| `time_average(freq='D', data_thresh=0.75)` | 10⁻¹² µg/m³ | ✅ Pass |
| `time_average(freq='MS', data_thresh=0.75)` | 10⁻¹² µg/m³ | ✅ Pass |
| `time_average(statistic='percentile', percentile=95)` | 10⁻¹² µg/m³ | ✅ Pass |
| `trend(avg_time='month', deseason=False)` slope | 10⁻² µg/m³/yr | ✅ Pass |
| `trend(...)` significance at α=0.05 | boolean agreement | ✅ Pass |
| `trend(...)` CI inclusion of zero | boolean agreement | ✅ Pass |
| `timeVariation` hour / day-of-week / month means | 10⁻¹⁰ µg/m³ | ✅ Pass |
| `time_average(freq='W-MON')` | label alignment deferred | ⏸ Pending |

Each row is gated by a CI test in `tests/test_openair_parity.py`; if
this page renders, every listed metric is passing. More metrics will be
added as aeolus's metrics module grows — each extension is a fixture, a
pytest case, and a narrative section here.
